findings.title: Spec table doesn't call out that retro --rewrite fails (not asks) on a held lock
findings.detail: The command table row says `takt retro --rewrite` "takes the session lock (§4.6) as `next` does", but §4.6 describes the lock's only documented behaviour on contention as `ask: owner` (take over / abort / read-only). The diff (internal/cli/cmd_next.go's new nextRun.lockBlocked/blockedBy, and internal/cli/cmd_retro.go's retroLockHeld) makes retro --rewrite diverge on exactly this point: a live holder makes it fail outright (exitError, naming the holder and hinting `takt unlock`), never asking. That divergence is well explained in the new code's doc comments, but the spec — which is otherwise very precise about command-specific exceptions (e.g. the push_pr no-op rule two rows above) — doesn't mention it, so a reader relying on the table/§4.6 alone would expect retro --rewrite to print the same owner-ask question next does.
